algorithm.Title: Postpartum - C-section Symptoms - Female (Adult)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Adult | Female
Definition: C-section recovery symptom assessment decomposed from NHS.UK's published C-section recovery guidance.
FirstAid: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 now. Do not drive yourself. Tell the call handler about the recent C-section. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Is this a skin wound or injury unrelated to a recent C-section?
questions.Information: A non-operative skin wound or injury belongs in the Skin Injury pathway.

questions.Question: Is there trouble breathing, chest pain, fainting, heavy or gushing vaginal bleeding, confusion, or rapidly worsening severe pain or illness?
questions.Information: Breathing difficulty, chest pain, fainting, heavy bleeding, confusion, or rapidly worsening illness are urgent maternal warning signs requiring immediate emergency care.

questions.Question: Is the wound increasingly red, painful, swollen, opening, or draining pus or foul-smelling fluid; is there fever, persistent severe incision pain, painful urination, or leaking urine without the emergency features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance lists wound infection and urinary symptoms after a C-section as requiring prompt clinical review.

questions.Question: Is this normal, expected C-section recovery with none of the features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance describes routine wound care and gradual activity increase as the expected recovery path.

advice.Title: Emergency C-section complication precautions
Content: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 now. Do not drive yourself. Tell the call handler about the recent C-section. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: worsening pain or bleeding; breathing difficulty.

advice.Title: Urgent C-section complication review
Content: Arrange prompt clinical assessment through the locally approved Qatar maternity pathway; the exact non-emergency destination remains GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED.
Call Back If: symptoms worsen; fever develops.

advice.Title: Home care for normal C-section recovery
Content: Follow the discharge team's wound-care and activity instructions. Keep the wound clean and dry, use sanitary pads rather than tampons, and increase gentle activity gradually. A clinician or pharmacist should confirm any pain medicine is suitable for this patient, including during breastfeeding.
Call Back If: wound becomes red, painful, swollen, opens, or drains fluid; fever, heavy bleeding, chest pain, breathing difficulty, or one-sided leg pain develops.

references: NHS.UK, "Caesarean section - Recovery", https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/caesarean-section/recovery/ (page last reviewed 04 January 2023)
